w10_T4_005263: Amira designed 151 enamel badges for the club fair. The printer produced 3 copies of every one of them, so her stock tripled overnight. Her teammate Josef, whose own design had sold far fewer, contributed 27 badges from his box. The stall was open for 4 days on the seafront. Every badge in the crate is supplied with 6 fastening pins, and the organisers handed Amira 49 loose pins from the stores. How many fastening pins did Amira have?
w10_T4_005266: The phone shop had 14 display handsets on its counter when it opened in the morning, and the tariffs there are quoted in minutes rather than in hours. A queue of early customers bought 13 of the handsets before the manager arrived. The shop discovered that 4 chargers were boxed with every handset still on the counter. During the afternoon a wholesaler delivered 54 more chargers. In the evening a repair shop returned 8 chargers it had borrowed. How many chargers did the shop have?
w10_T4_005272: The tile showroom had 150 boxes in its back room and took delivery of 68 more on Monday. Every box in the back room contains 4 glazed tiles, and the shop quotes areas in square centimetres rather than in square metres. A fitter added 77 loose tiles from a broken pallet to the same count. A kitchen job used 630 tiles, and a bathroom refit took another 202. The showroom is 30 metres long. A customer then returned 65 unopened tiles. How many tiles were in the back room afterwards?
w10_T4_005273: Elias keeps 19 sheets of old stamps in a folder, and each sheet is divided into 6 blocks. Every block on those sheets holds 8 separate stamps, and half of them come from countries that no longer exist. His aunt Marisol, whose own album is much thinner than his folder, gave him 11 loose stamps for his birthday. At a collectors fair Elias traded away 809 stamps for a single rare cover. How many stamps did Elias have left?
w10_T4_005274: The theatre wardrobe held 143 costumes at the end of the run. A touring company borrowed 137 of them for a production in another city. A dozen dressers work backstage on a busy night. Every costume still hanging in the wardrobe needs 6 replacement buttons before the revival. The head of wardrobe found 53 matching buttons in her sewing box and added them. She then used 40 of the buttons on a long coat for the lead. How many buttons were left?
w10_T4_005276: The snack factory started the morning with 157 sacks of roasted nuts and took in 61 more from the drying floor. Every sack is emptied into 4 mixing tubs on the line. Each tub is portioned into 5 retail bags, and the factory prints its weights in grams rather than in kilograms. During the afternoon each bag was found to hold 2 sealed sachets. In the evening the labelling machine put 3 stickers on every sachet. How many stickers did the machine use?
w10_T4_005277: The choir library held 217 sheets of music before the summer concert. The conductor sent 109 of the sheets to the county archive for safekeeping. Every sheet that stayed was copied 6 times for the singers. Bea and her fellow librarian Nils then divided all the copies equally among the 3 voice sections, and Bea took charge of the set for the sopranos, which Nils agreed was the largest job of the three. Each copy in that set runs to 9 printed pages. How many printed pages were in the sopranos' set?
w10_T4_005279: A tool hire depot owns 147 aluminium ladders, and it lists ladder heights in centimetres rather than in metres. At the annual audit 25 ladders were out on long hire and were excluded. Another 39 ladders were sold off as too worn to keep. The depot runs 6 vans from its yard. Every ladder that remained was examined at 9 separate safety points. The inspector recorded 191 of those checks as failures. How many of the checks were passes?
w10_T4_005280: The council planted 204 flower beds in the park last autumn, and 6 tulips went into every bed. Half of the beds lie along the edge of the lake. A hard frost in February killed 221 of the tulips. The parks team replanted 45 tulips in the gaps as soon as the ground softened. The park itself covers 15 hectares. Every tulip that flowered opened with 8 petals, and the show display in the glasshouse contributed 79 further petals to the count. How many petals were counted in the park?
w10_T4_005287: Farid booked 211 minutes of recording time at the studio, which bills its work in minutes rather than in hours. The manager added 19 minutes for free after a power cut. Farid used 133 minutes on the drum takes and another 63 on the vocals. Mixing the first single took a further 25 minutes. His engineer Nia, who had booked far more time than he had, transferred 55 minutes from her own block to his account. How many minutes did Farid have left?
w10_T4_005291: The youth club owned 86 board games at the start of the year, and it times its sessions in minutes rather than in hours. It lent 40 of the games permanently to a hospital play room. Half of the games in the cupboard are for two players only. Parents donated 15 games in the spring, and the club bought 63 more at a closing-down sale. The leader then shared all the games equally among the 4 branch clubs and drove one branch's share across town. How many games did that branch receive?
w10_T4_005293: A second-hand bookshop had 191 crates of stock in its cellar and bought 26 more from a house clearance. Every crate holds 8 books once they are unpacked. Each book was listed on 4 separate online marketplaces by the shop assistant. The owner added 13 listings that he typed in by hand for rare items. Over the year 3451 of the listings expired without a sale and were taken down. How many listings were still live?
w10_T4_005294: The school hired 3 coaches for the field trip, and each coach carried 148 pupils and their bags. The journey to the coast is 120 kilometres each way. A further 65 pupils travelled by train and joined the group at the station. Every pupil on the trip was handed 7 activity vouchers at the entrance. Each voucher is worth 8 points in the end-of-term prize scheme. How many points were handed out in total?
w10_T4_005297: A soap workshop made 46 batches of lavender soap last month, and every batch sets into 5 solid blocks. A trial run added 21 further blocks, and a partner workshop sent over 71 blocks of its own. The workshop weighs its oils in grams rather than in kilograms. Every block on the cutting bench is sliced into 4 bars. The store room also held 29 finished bars from the previous month. How many bars did the workshop have?
w10_T4_005302: A tree nursery filled 209 trays for the reforestation scheme, and each tray was sown with 6 seedlings. Half of the seedlings were driven up to the northern site, and half stayed in the propagation shed. The site has 7 greenhouses along its southern fence. Every seedling left in the shed grew 5 leaves by midsummer. An infestation of caterpillars then stripped 1902 leaves from the trays. How many leaves were left in the shed?
w10_T4_005303: A market gardener grows lettuce in 47 long rows, with 7 heads standing in every row. She cut 33 additional heads from the cold frame by the wall. The van she uses was bought 9 years ago. Over the weekend 296 heads were sold at the farmers market. Early on Monday she cut 68 more heads and added them to the pile. The pile was then divided equally between 2 delivery crates, and the crate for the restaurant was loaded first. How many heads of lettuce were in the restaurant's crate?
w10_T4_005304: The museum printed 180 fundraising booklets for its winter appeal and found 38 more left from last year. Every booklet contains 5 tear-out coupons. Half of the coupons were sold at the front desk, and half stayed in the office. The trustees gave 360 of the office coupons to corporate sponsors. The printer then supplied 76 replacement coupons, and 50 unused coupons came back from a school. How many coupons did the office have?
w10_T4_005306: The quiz league had 139 question cards in its box, and a dozen teams take part each season. The committee withdrew 48 cards that had appeared too often, and Ivan, who writes far more cards than his colleague Petra, agreed with her decision. Every card still in the box carries 6 separate questions. Over the season 421 of those questions were read out in matches. Each question that was never used is worth 6 points in the reserve round. How many points are held in the reserve round?
w10_T4_005314: The cobbler had 83 pairs of leather laces hanging behind the counter, and he gives all lace lengths in centimetres rather than in metres. Customers bought 60 pairs during the winter sale. A supplier then delivered 35 more pairs. Since every pair contains 2 separate laces, the number of individual laces on the hook is double the number of pairs. The cobbler used 45 of those individual laces on repairs during February. How many individual laces were left?
w10_T4_005322: A fruit trader arrived at the market in the morning with 64 punnets of strawberries. He shared them equally among the 4 stalls his family runs, and he stayed all day at the stall in the square. Before noon 12 of the punnets at his stall were sold to a café. During the afternoon 2 more punnets went to a passing shopper. In the evening a neighbour bought 1 punnet just as he was packing up. How many punnets did he take home from his stall?
w10_T4_005323: The delivery depot runs 18 vans on weekdays, and each van completes 5 rounds in a day. Dana plans the routes and her colleague Ravi checks them, and Dana always ends up with more streets on her sheet than Ravi has on his. Every round takes in 5 streets, and each street on the map holds 6 houses. The depot logs its distances in metres rather than in kilometres. Each house receives 3 leaflets on the campaign day. How many leaflets are delivered on the campaign day?
w10_T4_005325: The warehouse held 214 sacks of rice when it opened in the morning. Half of them were sent straight down to the docks, and half stayed on the floor. A lorry, which holds 40 sacks when full, delivered 55 more during the morning. At midday the stock on the floor was divided equally between 2 town stores, and the manager travelled with the load for the High Street store. That store sold 25 sacks over the afternoon and took back 22 sacks from a cancelled order. In the evening every sack in the High Street store was split into 3 retail bags. How many retail bags did the High Street store have?
w10_T4_005327: The campsite bought in 102 bundles of firewood before the bank holiday. The warden shared the bundles equally among the 3 camping fields and then looked after the west field himself. Rain got into the store there and ruined 1 bundle, which he threw on the compost. A supplier dropped off 69 more bundles at the west field on the Saturday. Campers burned 77 bundles over the long weekend. How many bundles were left in the west field?
w10_T4_005329: The old cinema has 30 rows in its main screen, and every row holds 7 seats. Half of the screenings in the season are matinees. Ola manages the box office and Yusuf the projection room, and between them they booked every seat in the house for each of the 8 screenings in the festival. The theatre then sold 77 standing tickets at the back of the hall. Yusuf reserved 28 further places for the staff and their guests. How many places were taken in total?
w10_T4_005331: A collector had 122 vinyl records stacked along his living room wall. He sold 110 of them to a dealer who came with a van. The record shop in town has 3 listening booths. Every record he kept came with 2 printed inserts inside the sleeve. He mislaid 16 of the inserts during a house move. Sorting through a box, he found 5 more inserts he had forgotten about, and he later gave 12 inserts to a friend who was framing them. How many inserts did the collector still have?
